description: UNESCO World Heritage Sites located in Maharashtra, India (5 sites). Subset of the national `hi-unesco-world-heritage-sites` flagship; filter applied: state == "Maharashtra". Sourced from Kushwahaabhay/UNESCO-Site-Finder (MIT, 2025-11).

rows.name: Ajanta Caves
rows.description: Rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE. Famous for their ancient paintings and sculptures.

rows.name: Ellora Caves
rows.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments carved out of rock. Includes the famous Kailasa temple.

rows.name: Elephanta Caves
rows.description: A network of sculpted caves on Elephanta Island. Famous for rock-cut art and sculptures dedicated to Lord Shiva.

rows.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
rows.description: A historic railway station in Mumbai and an outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture.

rows.name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
rows.description: A collection of 19th-century Victorian Gothic and 20th-century Art Deco buildings. Unique blend of architectural styles.
